chapter: Taped excerpts: friends, family and facts
title: Fats and James P. Johnson playing together
summary: Johnson cannot recall the club; Rasch relays that he said he got his left hand from Fats, who got it from James P.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Frank, uh-huh. Once you were talking with Tom about you and Fats Waller and J. P. Johnson going to some club or some little spot and all three of you playing with Fats hitting a chord and taking off and then somebody else picking up on it. Do you recall what club that was?
Do you recall, do you remember doing that?
Do you remember, you know, the three of you getting together and making music together?
Well, I go along (inaudible). It's hard to I don't even recollect.
J. C., like all of us, has his up and down days. Regarding James P. Johnson and Fats, if you can get through the haze in tapes 3, 4 and 5, which was the
newspaper interview that I taped, he mentions James P. Johnson and Fats. He said that he got his left hand from Fats, and Fats got it from James P., and that's the chain of command there.
I'm going to continue with some excerpts from other tapes, and we'll just get bits and pieces together which may connect.
